## NCLEX To‑Do List (from today to test day)

### 1) Set up your plan (Day 0–1)
- [ ] Pick your NCLEX test date (or target date) and register with Pearson VUE  
- [ ] Confirm your ATT, ID requirements, and testing center rules  
- [ ] Choose **one primary question bank** (e.g., UWorld, Archer, Kaplan, etc.)  
- [ ] Choose **one content resource** (e.g., Saunders, Simple Nursing, Mark Klimek notes/lectures)  
- [ ] Set a weekly schedule (minimum 5 days/week)

### 2) Build your daily routine (Weeks 1–4+)
**Daily (or study-day) checklist**
- [ ] Do **75–125 NCLEX-style questions** (timed once you’re comfortable)  
- [ ] Review every rationale (right and wrong) and write 5–15 “takeaways”  
- [ ] Make a short “weak topics” list (labs, meds, diseases, prioritization errors)  
- [ ] Do **20–30 minutes** of focused content review based on missed questions  
- [ ] Practice **NGN-style** (case studies, SATA, bow-tie, matrix) every study day

### 3) Master high-yield NCLEX skills (ongoing)
- [ ] Prioritization & delegation (RN vs LPN vs UAP; unstable vs stable; ABCs)  
- [ ] Safety & infection control (PPE, isolation, falls, restraints)  
- [ ] Med safety basics (high-alert meds, insulin, anticoagulants, opioids)  
- [ ] Critical labs & trends (K+, Na+, glucose, INR, creatinine, ABGs basics)  
- [ ] Therapeutic communication (what to say/avoid; suicide precautions)  
- [ ] Maternity/newborn essentials (postpartum hemorrhage, preeclampsia, newborn complications)  
- [ ] Peds essentials (dehydration, respiratory distress signs, dosing safety)

### 4) Weekly checkpoints (every 7 days)
- [ ] Take **1 full-length practice exam** or 2–3 “readiness” assessments  
- [ ] Analyze results: top 3 weak areas + top 3 recurring error types  
- [ ] Adjust the next week’s plan to attack those weaknesses  
- [ ] Do one “mixed” question day to mimic the real exam (all subjects)

### 5) Two weeks before test day
- [ ] Switch most question sets to **timed, mixed, 85–150 questions**  
- [ ] Do at least **2 NGN case studies** per week (more if available)  
- [ ] Review your notes/“missed question” notebook daily  
- [ ] Identify your “red flag” topics and do targeted drills (20–40 Q each)

### 6) Final week
- [ ] Do 1–2 final assessments (don’t cram endlessly)  
- [ ] Review only high-yield notes and recurring mistakes  
- [ ] Confirm testing appointment, route, parking, and required ID  
- [ ] Set sleep schedule to match test day

### 7) Day before + test day
**Day before**
- [ ] No heavy studying (light review only if it calms you)  
- [ ] Pack ID, snacks, water, layers, confirmation email  
- [ ] Plan breakfast and timing  
- [ ] Go to bed early

**Test day**
- [ ] Arrive early  
- [ ] Use breaks strategically (hydrate, reset)  
- [ ] Focus on: safety, priority, “what kills first,” and least/most appropriate actions

---

## Quick questions so I can tailor this to you
1) When is your test (or how many weeks out)?  
2) What resources do you have (UWorld/Archer/Kaplan/Saunders/etc.)?  
3) Are you stronger in content or test-taking (prioritization/strategy)?
